scenes.heading: Converting fractions, decimals and percentages
scenes.say: Twelve and a half per cent. Two hundred and fifty per cent. Point seven five per cent. Fine print is full of awkward numbers like these. Today you'll learn to convert any of them between fractions, decimals and percentages.
scenes.caption: 12½%. 250%. 0.75%. Fine print is full of awkward numbers like these. Today you'll learn to convert any of them between fractions, decimals and percentages.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Dollars, euros and yen: same value, different currency
scenes.breaks: Real exchange rates change every day. These conversions never change: 1/4 is always 25%.
scenes.say: Think of fractions, decimals and percentages as three currencies. The value stays the same; only the way it's written changes. To compare prices, you'd change everything into dollars. To compare numbers, change everything into one form.
scenes.caption: Think of fractions, decimals and percentages as three currencies. The value stays the same; only the way it's written changes. To compare numbers, change everything into one form.

scenes.heading: The conversion map
scenes.say: Here's your map. Percentage to decimal: divide by one hundred, so two hundred and fifty per cent is two point five. Decimal to percentage: multiply by one hundred. Percentage to fraction: put it over one hundred and simplify. Fraction to percentage: multiply by one hundred per cent. And remember, one hundred per cent is one whole.
scenes.caption: Percentage to decimal: ÷ 100, so 250% = 2.5. Decimal to percentage: × 100. Percentage to fraction: over 100 and simplify. Fraction to percentage: × 100%. 100% is one whole.

scenes.heading: Beyond one whole
scenes.say: Here one whole is one hundred per cent, so one and three quarters is one hundred and seventy-five per cent.
scenes.caption: One whole is 100%, so 1¾ is 175%.

scenes.heading: A fractional percentage
scenes.question: Write 12½% as a fraction in simplest form.
scenes.say: Twelve and a half per cent as a fraction. Put it over one hundred: twelve point five over one hundred. There's a decimal inside, so multiply top and bottom by ten: one hundred and twenty-five over one thousand. Divide both by one hundred and twenty-five, and you get one eighth.
scenes.caption: 12½% as a fraction. Over 100: 12.5/100. There's a decimal inside, so × 10 top and bottom: 125/1000. Divide both by 125, and you get 1/8.

scenes.heading: A recurring decimal
scenes.question: Write 5/6 as a percentage, exactly.
scenes.say: Five sixths as a percentage. Multiply by one hundred per cent: five hundred over six, which is two hundred and fifty thirds. Two hundred and fifty divided by three is eighty-three remainder one. So it's exactly eighty-three and a third per cent, or about eighty-three point three.
scenes.caption: 5/6 as a percentage. × 100%: 500/6 = 250/3. 250 ÷ 3 = 83 remainder 1. So it's exactly 83⅓%, or about 83.3%.

scenes.heading: Match the units first
scenes.question: Write 80 cm as a percentage of 15 m.
scenes.say: Eighty centimetres as a percentage of fifteen metres. First, match the units: fifteen metres is fifteen hundred centimetres. Then part over whole, times one hundred per cent. That's sixteen thirds per cent, or five and a third per cent.
scenes.caption: 80 cm as a percentage of 15 m. First match the units: 15 m = 1500 cm. Then part over whole, × 100%. That's 16/3 %, or 5⅓%.

scenes.heading: Watch out
scenes.say: Watch out. Half a per cent is tiny: zero point zero zero five. One point five is one hundred and fifty per cent. Clear any decimals out of a fraction. And always match the units before you divide.

Quick recap. Divide by one hundred to get a decimal, multiply by one hundred to get a percentage. One hundred per cent is one whole. Clear decimals out of fractions. Thirds give thirty-three and a third, and sixty-six and two thirds per cent. And match units before you divide. Now try the practice questions!
scenes.caption: Quick recap. ÷ 100 to get a decimal, × 100 to get a percentage. 100% is one whole. Clear decimals out of fractions. Thirds: 33⅓% and 66⅔%. Match units before you divide. Now try the practice questions!
